synoptic.summary: A weak trough is sliding south of Utah into northern Mexico while a broad Pacific ridge builds over the top: dry, no showers or thunderstorms (0% precipitation and thunder in every launch forecast), light terrain-driven winds. Winds aloft stay light the whole period (≤ 9 kt at 850 and 700 mb), so no mixing-down or strong-flow rotor problem. Friday a northerly gradient keeps north flow at Point of the Mountain all day — no south drainage this morning, a break from the usual pattern. Saturday is a textbook ridge day: light south drainage in the morning, switch to north around 14:00. Sunday the flow aloft backs to south-southwest (700 mb ~210° 8–9 kt) and the launch forecast stays south all day with no afternoon switch to north — another departure from the normal cycle, and the Cherry rotor trigger.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: With the presence of the ridge, winds will be generally light and terrain driven. However, the combination of a northerly pressure gradient and weak cold advection will bring some gusty winds to the prone gap areas of Washington county overnight into tomorrow morning.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure rose from 1018.4 mb (Thu 12:54) to 1026.0 mb (Fri 09:54) as the ridge builds; it eased 0.5 mb in the last hour, so the rise is levelling off. High pressure and a light gradient favour calm morning and evening windows.

observations.summary: As of ~09:55 MST, north flow on the Utah Valley side: Spanish Fork 359° 6 kt gusting 8, Alpine 318° 4 kt gusting 7, Lehi light west (251° 2 kt gusting 7), Provo calm. Salt Lake airport has light south drainage (180° 3 kt), so the transition zone sits north of Point of the Mountain and no south flow reaches POM South. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations; South Valley Regional's latest report (09:35) has no wind, its last wind reading is 330° 3 kt at 08:15 MST. Add 3–8 kt to valley readings to estimate launch wind.
